description: Nowhere in REQ-101 (lender eligibility, lines 266-336), REQ-102 (borrower eligibility, lines 386-406), REQ-105 (reputation-capital sizing ladder, lines 523-696), or REQ-111 (money-safety invariant, lines 1568-1591) does this spec require `lender_id !== borrower_id` for a candidate loan. A single self-funded citizen that is ALREADY solvent enough to pass REQ-101's lender-eligibility gate (available surplus > $0) has zero structural barrier to also satisfying REQ-102's borrower-eligibility gate for a loan FROM ITSELF, provided its own current balance happens to be below `BORROWER_LOW_USD` at evaluation time -- and even where that specific boundary condition doesn't hold today, the spec never states this exclusion as a design invariant, so nothing prevents it from becoming exploitable the moment any self-funded citizen's balance dips below $0.50 while it also has surplus reserved elsewhere, or if a future revision loosens REQ-102's threshold. Confirmed via grep across both specs/behavioral-spec.md and specs/verification-architecture.md this session: zero occurrences of any `lenderId`/`borrowerId` distinctness check, and zero occurrences of the phrase 'self-loan' or any equivalent exclusion. This matters because REQ-105's ENTIRE cold-start-resolution rationale rests on `successfulOnTimeRepayments` (`countSuccessfulOnTimeRepayments(loanRows, borrowerId)`, lines 537-542) being a genuine, hard-won track record earned under REAL counterparty risk -- the doubling ladder (`computeLoanCapUsd`) and the kill-switch's own pause threshold (`evaluateColdStartKillSwitch`, gated on `computeColdStartRepaymentRate`) both implicitly assume a borrower's repayment count reflects actual risk survived. A self-funded citizen with zero real financial risk can trivially self-loan-and-self-repay through this SAME mechanism (it already controls both the lender's and the borrower's private keys) at negligible real cost -- REQ-104's smallest loan is $0.02 principal plus $0.002 interest, an amount any self-funded citizen can pay to itself with zero net loss -- repeating this 8 times (per PROP-105b's own boundary case) inflates that citizen's `successfulOnTimeRepayments` to the point where `computeLoanCapUsd` returns the full `maxLoanUsd=$5.00` ceiling, entirely without ever having survived a single loan from a genuine, independent counterparty. When this citizen SUBSEQUENTLY borrows from a REAL, separate lender, that lender's own REQ-101 surplus check and REQ-105 ladder-based sizing decision are both being fed a fabricated reputation signal, defeating the exact cold-start risk-mitigation guarantee this entire feature exists to provide (per the spec's own framing, 'the smallest mechanism that actually resolves the cold-start SIZING problem,' line 79-80) -- the REAL lender's downside is no longer 'structurally tiny by construction' (line 549) once the borrower's own claimed track record can be manufactured for free. This also silently corrupts `computeColdStartRepaymentRate`'s own monitoring signal (REQ-105's 'experimental hypothesis' tracking mechanism, lines 563-591): self-dealt loans would count toward `sampleSize`/`repaidCount` alongside genuine borrower-to-lender loans with zero way to distinguish them, systematically inflating the observed repayment rate above the TRUE rate for genuinely at-risk cold-start loans -- exactly the metric REQ-105's own kill-switch (`evaluateColdStartKillSwitch`) depends on to decide whether to pause new cold-start issuance.

evidence.snippet: REQ-101: WHEN a citizen is considered as a potential lender ... REQ-102: WHEN a citizen is considered as a potential borrower, THE SYSTEM SHALL admit it as eligible only if ALL THREE hold: (a) isSelfFunded() ... (b) its own current balance is strictly below BORROWER_LOW_USD ... (c) loans.jsonl contains NO row for that citizen (as borrower_id ...) -- no fourth condition anywhere requiring lender_id !== borrower_id

crossCheck.note: Grepped the full 149-line Proof Obligations table for 'self-loan', 'lenderId !== borrowerId', or any equivalent -- zero matches. No PROP anywhere requires or tests that a candidate loan's lender_id differs from its borrower_id, and no PROP tests that computeColdStartRepaymentRate's own sample excludes or flags self-dealt loans.
